title: Dobrushin uniqueness for the four-dimensional SU(2) Wilson lattice gauge measure for beta < 2/9, with interval/Lean certificates (note v1.6)
description:
Dobrushin uniqueness for the four-dimensional SU(2) Wilson lattice gauge measure for β < 2/9, with interval/Lean certificates (note v1.6, 12 November 2026; the previous versions are v1.5 of 1 November 2026, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23856414, and v1.4 of 28 October 2026, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23712954).

New in version 1.6. Literature corrections only; no theorem, proof, constant or certificate of the note is changed. The remark that global Bakry–Émery on link variables cannot pass β = 1/8 is restricted to the version without gauge fixing, and the gauge-fixed range βW < 4/29 of version 4.45.0 of the Bhattacharjee–Bhattacharya et al. series is recorded. The Zenodo creation dates of the versions of that series (2.0.0, 3.0.0, 4.45.0, 4.46.0) are given as dates of records, without any claim of priority. The Zenodo records of H. T. Rajabu (10.5281/zenodo.23691339 and 10.5281/zenodo.23729328) are cited with the statements of the author (uniqueness ranges, area law for βW < 2/3), whose proofs were not checked here, and the comparison with the area-law section and with Borgs–Seiler (1983) is written without a priority ranking. The elapsed time between records is corrected to about five days.

Result. For the SU(2) Wilson action on Z4 with weight exp(−β Σp(1 − ½ Re Tr Up)), the Gibbs (DLR) measure is unique for 0 ≤ β < 2/9 ≈ 0.222 (equivalently g2 > 18; βtH < 1/18 in the 't Hooft normalisation). Method: Dobrushin's criterion in its Wasserstein (W1) form with the Euclidean (chordal) metric of R4 on SU(2) ≅ S3, the metric used by Levin (1980). Secondary result: with the geodesic metric the exact coefficient is 8β/(9π), which gives the weaker range β < π/16. Each threshold is sharp for its criterion.

Content added in version 1.5 (kept). (1) The one-site coefficient in a field of strength κ equals Eκ[x⊥2] = I2(κ)/(κ I1(κ)) for every κ ≥ 0 (v1.4: κ ≤ 4/3); for κ > 0 the maximum over directions is attained exactly for the directions orthogonal to the field, oblique directions are strictly smaller with explicit two-sided bounds, and the coefficient is strictly decreasing in κ, hence maximal at zero field, where it equals 1/4. Each of the 18 neighbouring links has influence exactly β/4 and the Dobrushin sum is 9β/2. The proof is analytic (divergence-free flux field, slice estimate, exact sum-of-squares identity, Chebyshev association argument); it is not formalised in Lean. The interval-arithmetic proof of v1.4 on κ ≤ 4/3, with its Lean-checked final steps, is kept as a second proof (Appendix A). (2) A corollary records the Poincaré inequality for β < 2/9, uniform in the volume and the boundary condition, that Wu's theorem (2006) gives from these coefficients (a corollary, not a new method). (3) Application (Section 7 and Appendix B): the same chordal coefficient, applied to the slab σ-models of Durhuus and Fröhlich through Dobrushin's comparison, gives Wilson's area law for β < 2/3, uniformly on tori, with free boundary conditions and for every Gibbs measure, with string tension at least arcosh(2/β − 2). This range is not new: Borgs and Seiler (1983, Appendix B of the preprint version) proved confinement for β < 12/17 by a transfer-matrix argument, and no priority is claimed for any threshold; the contribution is an independent proof with explicit constants.

Prior public statement. The uniqueness range β < 2/9 for the four-dimensional SU(2) model (with exponential decay and a lattice mass gap), the all-field bound Dch(κ) ≤ 1/4, i.e. W1(νb, νb') ≤ |b − b'|/4 on S3 (Levin's Remark 3.7 for N = 4), and the exactness of the influence coefficient β/4 were stated publicly, with proofs, in the preprint of D. Bhattacharjee and U. Bhattacharya, “Mass Gap of Lattice Yang-Mills Theory up to the Dobrushin Ceiling”, hexagon:2610.00341v1, 18 October 2026 (Theorems E, F and 7 and Proposition 13; the same statement is Theorem 125 of v4, with J. M. Lockwood; Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.23786523). This note was prepared independently and makes no priority claim on them. Its own contributions: the exact value I2/(κ I1) of the supremum over directions for every κ ≥ 0, its maximisers, the two-sided estimate for oblique directions, the strict monotonicity in κ and an analytic proof; the exact geodesic coefficient 8β/(9π); two interval-arithmetic certificates with independent checks; Lean-checked final steps; explicit transfers of the published constants of Levin, Royer and Shen-Zhu-Zhu to the Wilson link; and the area-law application (an independent proof; the range itself is not new).

Status. The chordal identity for all κ is proved on paper by an analytic argument, not formalised in Lean, read by one independent reviewer (a language model) and not refereed; the area-law application of Section 7 and Appendix B is also proved on paper only, not formalised, and was read by the same reviewer; numerical and interval cross-checks (exact power series to κ39, Arb at 90 digits, interval certificates on [4/3, 20], optimal transport) are not used in the proof. The v1.4 proof on κ ≤ 4/3 (Arb interval arithmetic, independent mpmath recertification, final rational steps checked in Lean 4, Mathlib v4.34.0, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only) is kept as a second proof. The archive contains the note (PDF and LaTeX), the certificates with reproduction scripts, the independent checks, the cross-check scripts for Sections 4 and 7 and a standalone Lean project that builds from scratch.

Limitations. Uniqueness, the Poincaré inequality of the corollary and the area law of Section 7 for rectangular Wilson loops (range not new); no other decay of correlations, no transfer-matrix gap and no log-Sobolev inequality is claimed. The Borgs–Seiler threshold was read in the preprint version only. The geodesic bound is certified only for κ ≤ 59/50. Prior art: Levin (1980), Royer (1986), Gross (1979), Simon (1979) and Wu (2006) were read; the bound 1/4 for all fields and the range 2/9 are in the preprint of Bhattacharjee and Bhattacharya. Not consulted: Seiler's monograph (LNP 159), the content of Georgii's book, Simon's book on lattice gases, the journal version of Borgs–Seiler, and Brydges–Giffen–Durhuus–Fröhlich (1986) beyond its abstract. A strong-coupling statement: nothing is claimed about the continuum limit or the Yang–Mills mass gap.

Prepared with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic); the analytic proof (Section 4) and the area-law section (Section 7, Appendix B) were read by an independent reviewer, Kimi K3.1 Pro (Moonshot AI), a language model; every claim in the note carries a status label.
